title: UIDAI Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) on Demographic Exception and Cross-Limit Updates
section: Cross-Limit Exception Handling for Name and Gender Lifetime Limits
text:
Statutory Demographic Update Limits: Under UIDAI enrolment regulations, demographic updates are subject to strict lifetime quotas: Name can be updated a maximum of twice (2 times); Gender can be updated only once (1 time). When a resident exhausts these statutory limits, self-service portal updates are blocked with an error. 

Root Cause: Identity drift and attempting to update demographic fields online after exhausting the statutory lifetime update quota. 

Direct Resolution via Regional Office (RO) Exception Workflow: 1. Visit an authorized Aadhaar Seva Kendra (ASK) and request an update. The center will generate an Enrolment Identification (EID) packet slip which will get rejected by the automated backend due to limit exhaustion. 2. Collect the rejected EID slip and prepare mandatory evidentiary proof: For Name cross-limit, a formal Central or State Gazette Notification along with supporting civil records is mandatory. For Gender cross-limit, a medical certificate by a civil surgeon is required. 3. Submit a formal appeal to the jurisdictional UIDAI Regional Office (RO) attaching the EID slip, Gazette notification, and a written explanation requesting cross-limit approval under UIDAI Circular dated 28.10.2021. The Regional Office conducts a verification review to authorize the reprocessing of the rejected EID packet. 

Statutory TAT & Escalation: Regional Offices process exception requests within 30 to 90 working days. If no resolution is received within 30 days, call UIDAI Toll-Free 1947 or escalate via pgportal.gov.in (CPGRAMS).

title: UIDAI Standard Operating Procedure for Date of Birth (DoB) Cross-Limit Corrections
section: Date of Birth (DoB) Cross-Limit Exception Update and Birth Certificate Evidentiary Protocols
text:
Statutory Date of Birth (DoB) Update Quota: Under UIDAI regulations, Date of Birth (DoB) adjustments are restricted to a single update (1 time), provided the declared age does not deviate by more than three years (+/- 3 years) from the originally registered record. When the statutory limit is exhausted or deviation exceeds 3 years, online and ASK portal updates are rejected. 

Root Cause: Attempting to update Date of Birth beyond the single statutory lifetime limit or exceeding the 3-year age variance limit. 

Direct Resolution via Regional Office Exception Process: 1. Visit an authorized Aadhaar Seva Kendra (ASK) and submit a DoB update request to generate an Enrolment Identification (EID) slip (which will be initially rejected by the backend). 2. Mandatory Documentary Proof: A valid Birth Certificate issued by the competent authority (Registrar of Births and Deaths or Municipal Corporation) is strictly mandatory. School certificates or affidavits are not accepted for cross-limit DoB updates. 3. Draft a formal representation to the UIDAI Regional Office (RO) explaining the genuine circumstances, attaching the EID slip and self-attested copy of the Birth Certificate. 4. Submit via email or in person to the Regional Office. Upon field verification, the Regional Office approves the cross-limit exception on the backend. 

Statutory TAT & Escalation: Regional Offices process exception reviews within 30 to 90 days. For queries, contact UIDAI Toll-Free 1947.

title: UIDAI Biometric Locking and Error 330 Resident Authentication Resolution
section: Biometric Authentication Failure (Error 330) and Unlock Procedure under Regulation 11
text:
Biometric Authentication Failure (Error 330): Error 330 occurs when resident biometric authentication is attempted on POS devices, ATMs, or ration shops while the resident's biometrics are locked in the CIDR database. 

Root Cause: Under Regulation 11 of the Aadhaar (Authentication) Regulations, citizens can permanently lock or temporarily unlock their biometrics via the myAadhaar portal or mAadhaar application. When locked, all fingerprint and iris authentication requests are rejected with Error 330 to prevent unauthorized transactions. 

Direct Resolution (How to Unlock): 1. Log in to the myAadhaar portal (myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in) using your 12-digit Aadhaar number and OTP sent to your registered mobile number, or use an Aadhaar Time-based One-Time Password (TOTP). 2. Click on 'Lock / Unlock Biometrics' on the dashboard. 3. Choose either 'Unlock Biometrics Temporarily' (unlocks biometrics for 10 minutes for immediate authentication, then automatically locks again) or 'Unlock Biometrics Permanently' (disables the biometric lock). 4. Alternatively, open the mAadhaar mobile app, swipe to your Aadhaar profile, select 'Biometric Settings', and tap 'Unlock Biometrics'. 

Statutory TAT & Escalation: Biometric unlocking reflects instantaneously across all UIDAI authentication servers. If Error 330 persists after unlocking, call UIDAI Toll-Free 1947 or visit an Aadhaar Seva Kendra for biometric re-capture.

title: UIDAI Regulations on Baal Aadhaar Biometric Exemption and Mandatory Biometric Updates (MBU)
section: Baal Aadhaar Biometric Exemption and MBU-1 & MBU-2 Schedules
text:
Baal Aadhaar Biometric Rules and Mandatory Updates: For minors under the age of five (Baal Aadhaar, issued with a blue card), biometric profiles are exempt from initial fingerprint and iris scans, linking identity solely to facial photograph and parental Aadhaar. 

Root Cause of Identity Suspension: UIDAI regulations mandate two successive Mandatory Biometric Updates (MBU) as the child grows: MBU-1 between ages 5 and 7, and MBU-2 between ages 15 and 17. Failure to complete these mandatory updates leads to administrative identity suspension, causing downstream rejections during educational admissions, competitive examinations, scholarship disbursements, and passport processing. 

Direct Resolution: 1. Locate the nearest authorized Aadhaar Seva Kendra (ASK) or bank/post office enrolment center via appointments.uidai.gov.in. 2. Take the child along with the original Aadhaar card and child's birth certificate or school ID. 3. The center operator captures all ten fingerprints, both iris scans, and a fresh facial photograph. 4. Collect the enrolment acknowledgement slip. Mandatory Biometric Updates (MBU-1 at age 5-7 and MBU-2 at age 15-17) are completely FREE OF COST. 

Statutory TAT: The biometric profile updates on the CIDR database within 7 to 15 working days. Check status online at myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in.

title: UIDAI Citizen's Charter: Service Delivery Standards, EID Lifecycle, and Grievance Workflows
section: Statutory Service Standards, Turnaround Times (TAT), and Resident Grievance Hierarchy
text:
UIDAI Citizen's Charter Service Standards: The UIDAI Citizen's Charter establishes service delivery commitments for all Aadhaar lifecycle operations across India. 

Statutory Turnaround Times (TAT): - New Aadhaar Enrolment: Up to 90 calendar days from the date of enrolment packet upload. - Demographic Updates (Name, Address, Mobile, Email): Up to 30 calendar days. - Biometric Updates (MBU, Photo, Fingerprints): Up to 30 calendar days. - Document Updates: Up to 30 calendar days. 

Resident Grievance Redressal Hierarchy: 1. Level 1 - Contact Center: Call Toll-Free 1947 (available in 12 languages) or email helpdesk@uidai.gov.in quoting 14-digit EID or 28-digit SRN. 2. Level 2 - Resident Portal Grievance: Lodge an online grievance on myaadhaar.uidai.gov.in under 'File a Complaint'. 3. Level 3 - Regional Office Public Grievance Officer: If unresolved within 15 days, escalate to the Assistant Director / Public Grievance Officer of the jurisdictional Regional Office. 4. Level 4 - CPGRAMS: Escalate to the Department of Administrative Reforms and Public Grievances at pgportal.gov.in.

title: UIDAI Payment Gateway Error and Aadhaar PVC Card Payment Reconciliation SOP
section: Money Deducted via UPI/Card but Service Request Number (SRN) Not Generated
text:
Aadhaar PVC Card Payment Failure & Reconciliation Protocol: Ordering an Aadhaar PVC card online incurs a statutory fee of Rs 50. In instances of payment gateway dropouts, bank server delays, or network timeouts, the resident's bank or UPI account is debited, but the myAadhaar portal displays 'Payment Failed' or does not generate a Service Request Number (SRN). 

Root Cause: Asynchronous transaction processing between third-party UPI applications or payment aggregators and the government payment gateway, resulting in an unconsummated order state. 

Direct Resolution Steps: 1. Automated Reconciliation Window (24 to 48 Hours): Do NOT place a second order immediately. UIDAI and the payment gateway run automated settlement batches twice daily. If the transaction clears during batch reconciliation, the SRN is generated and an SMS confirmation with the 28-digit SRN is sent to your registered mobile number. 2. Auto-Refund for Failed Orders: If the transaction is flagged as un-reconciled, the payment aggregator initiates an auto-refund. The Rs 50 amount is reversed back to the source bank account / UPI VPA within 5 to 7 working days. 3. Manual Escalation: If no SRN or refund is received after 48 hours, contact UIDAI Helpdesk via Toll-Free 1947 or email helpdesk@uidai.gov.in. Provide your bank UTR / UPI Transaction Reference Number, date and exact time of payment, and masked Aadhaar number. 

Delivery TAT: Once the SRN is generated, UIDAI prints the PVC card within 5 working days and dispatches it via India Post Speed Post.
